submarine-yellow.prompt:
Create a better finished design for the object in the first attached native export, in the user's warm, softly lit cartoon style. The second image is a style reference for light, color and finish.

Use the source as a starting point, with creative freedom to improve the modeling. You may reshape forms and proportions, repair awkward construction, replace weak structural choices, add crafted details and decorations, and make the object richer and more appealing. Choose changes that improve its readable silhouette, volume, material separation and character at game scale. Do not merely repaint the same low-detail model, and do not preserve flawed geometry or an exact part count for its own sake. Keep it recognizable in its gameplay role and palette family.

Aim for soft rounded volumes, broad warm light, detailed but controlled edge reflections, readable midtones and deliberate materials. Decorations should belong to the object and support a coherent design, rather than filling every empty area. Avoid noisy photographic microtexture and glare that hides form.

Keep the supplied camera/projection, occupied grid scale, ground anchor, overall usable canvas and transparent composition. Keep gameplay attachment/contact points and functional clearances. For modular assets, lock the declared connection planes, end profiles, repeat scale and continuity with neighboring modules; redesign the interior and non-connecting surfaces freely. Maintain balanced light without a preferred horizontal direction, and no directional ground cast shadow. Existing restaurant floor tiles are outside this redesign.

Deliver one transparent-background concept sprite of this object. No unrelated scene, characters, UI, labels, accidental text, external halo or bloom. This is an ambitious design target for a native asset editor (Blender for 3D objects; the existing 2D pipeline for flat artwork), who can rebuild and refine the asset to realize the useful improvements while preserving the game's technical contract.
